Aggregators of the slot following the missed slot will be able to recursively aggregate the global proof from the missed slot into their subnet or global proof (leanVM is capable of doing recursive aggregation of proofs with different attestation data) As long as at least one aggregator performs such aggregation we are good. Such proof should be considered as better proof than just proof for the current slot attestations when it is picked by next proposer The current spec doesn't allow for aggregators to aggregate different heads. I kinda get it cause we don't really want to change the attestation object over p2p, just the signature. But this means among other things that this aggregating of previous proofs is not allowed. Otoh I believe DC will need this anyway We don't want to change aggregation object because it is too invasive change? Also it seems to me that if we allow aggregators to aggregate different heads, we may as well not have committees for aggregating, just allow aggregators to put whatever they've seen Interesting. Then we don't even need global topic for aggregation And then aggregators are subscribed to all subnets? We do, the proposer needs to get everything Not necessarily you can keep subnets, but many aggregators are subscribed to all subnets anyway So you just allow them to aggregate from any If we allow aggregators to aggregate anything (no matter for which slot) then they can just as well aggregate all current slots committees which is what proposer wants Yes that's what I'm saying Then we can just have a single topic for all types of aggregates. But we will need to update the aggregation message to allow having multiple attestation objects and multiple committee bits set (this is not possible today as I understand) > lower security: yep, there's a reason we do multi-path diffusion I thought the gossip mechanism is for security in the first place. Multi-path diffusion is for better latency mainly as far as I see it. Would it be reasonable for proposer of slot N+2 optimistically run recursion for slot N aggregates and include the product of it in the pool? This could be a fallback for the situation when slot N+1 proposer was unable to include enough aggregates or missed its proposal at all. yes this is the current design as far as I know However, it doesn't help with propagating 64 aggregates (~19 Mib without gossipsub amplification) within 5s interval which is required for the fork choice. It seems like the only way would be to reduce a number of aggregators to 8 which might be possible if we reduce a number of committees to 8, have 1 aggregator per committee and rely on those that are subscribed to all subnets. This is assuming we don't increase bandwidth requirements and use gossipsub from the security and robustness point of view push and announce is no difference. They are both potential diffusion paths. The latter is only realized if needed, in exchange for some latency. More generally I don't see how this is also not a problem in DC. In principle it can be made in a more streamlined way, but still in average we will need to aggregate the same number of attestations per slot and if we also want to include votes in blocks then it may be even worse. As far as I can see the network traffic for aggregations is the bigger blocker for Gasper but it's not obvious to me if it becomes much better on DC One thing that is in the back of my head is that if we decide to switch to DC, it could be simpler to start with a longer finality and just make less attesters per block, presumably having them all in the same topic and having very few aggregators yesh, it's not a problem in a way that attestations aren't critical to the fork choice in DC My codex is saying that 28 subnets with 1 aggregator each, 1 second for attestation broadcast then 3 seconds for aggregation and then 5 seconds to broadcast aggregates would be the most optimal in terms of bandwidth consumption between the attestation and aggregation phases -- they are almost even; I know it's a bad metric but that's at least something. I am using the time to aggregate and the size of aggregates from the <#1572284542990155908> . The closest would be 32 subnets and 1 aggregate, it slightly worse at the aggregation bandwidth part. 16 subnets gives a worse result because it takes more time to produce an aggregate thus less time for the broadcast how many validators can we have at most per subnet? we have roughly 32k validators per slot its closer to 25k on mainnet rn one second for attestation broadcast is probably too optimistic I would expect 2-3 seconds just my gut feeling it's not about just attestation broadcast, it's about atts broadcast + time to aggregate + time to broadcast aggregates all at once currently most attestations are seen within 1-1.5s of block receipt and then another significant group in the ~0.5s after the 4s cuttoff. E.g.: https://lab.ethpandaops.io/ethereum/slots/15682213?tab=attestations for 30k validators we can have the following: 16 subnets with 1 aggregator each, 2s to atts broadcast, 5s to aggregate, 2s to broadcast aggregates. I would add still have some slack on top of 25k that we have today isn't 1 aggregator per subnet super risky? On this, my current view is that with DC we can reduce network load in three meaningful ways: 1. Vote from the start of the slot, so we gain 3s per slot (with Gasper worst case attestation propagation start at t=3s) 2. We can pipeline, so no more dead time on the network while aggregation happens - and no more dead time on CPU while aggregations are broadcast 3. We can afford to have more optimistic assumptions, without negative impact on fork choice: For example, we can have less aggregators, and if an aggregate is missing, later aggregators can pick up the slack caveat: what's optimized here is the bandwidth for atts and aggs broadcast yes it is, if some aggregators can be subscribed to all subnets and produce aggregates for all of them this can be mitigated with 2 aggregators things become much worse in terms of bandwidth are aggregates signed by the aggreagator? or is it already the case that anyone can aggregate and gossip if they want to? it's still signed by aggregators ok but relax the requirement to be a member of the committee? seems like that could increase traffic a lot, if there are lots of 'volunteers' it should still be a selected aggregator, not a volunteer, otherwise it's gonna be a DoS vector Previously we discussed that only subnet aggregators are eligible to produce global proofs with assumption that with 4 aggregators per subnet we will have some aggregator with high stake which is subscribed to all subnets anyway. If we switch to 1 aggregator per subnet I am not sure if that assumption still holds, so we might need to rethink who is eligible to produce the global proof oh i see, so 1 of 16 is subscribed to all and aggregates all? The issue with this I think is that even if you have 64 cores or something on your machine you still cannot do 16 leaf aggregations in parallel b/c memory bandwidth becomes a bottleneck. A single leaf aggregation on leanVM currently reads / writes ~25GB/s to RAM which is approaching limits on most motherboards. so such large operators would need to be able to partition this work across multiple machines. oh, I didn't know about that limitation it seems like for both the leaf aggregations and the 16->1 it should be safe to use 'outside help' if it is available. Source the attestation aggregate from a large operator / provider - take the intersection of the attestations / clams you have and the aggregate has - verify the proof with the declared claims - this last produces a new proof but it is much faster then aggregating (~200ms or similar). <@857052906495017000> on the networking methodology, you mentioned having done something like this already IIUC. excerpts.author: yannvonlanthen
excerpts.content:
On this, my current view is that with DC we can reduce network load in three meaningful ways: 

1. Vote from the start of the slot, so we gain 3s per slot (with Gasper worst case attestation propagation start at t=3s)
2. We can pipeline, so no more dead time on the network while aggregation happens - and no more dead time on CPU while aggregations are broadcast
3. We can afford to have more optimistic assumptions, without negative impact on fork choice: For example, we can have less aggregators, and if an aggregate is missing, later aggregators can pick up the slack

excerpts.author: .just_kk

Previously we discussed that only subnet aggregators are eligible to produce global proofs with assumption that with 4 aggregators per subnet we will have some aggregator with high stake which is subscribed to all subnets anyway.

If we switch to 1 aggregator per subnet I am not sure if that assumption still holds, so we might need to rethink who is eligible to produce the global proof

excerpts.author: vladimir_ea
excerpts.content: oh i see, so 1 of 16 is subscribed to all and aggregates all? The issue with this I think is that even if you have 64 cores or something on your machine  you still cannot do 16 leaf aggregations in parallel b/c memory bandwidth becomes a bottleneck. A single leaf aggregation on leanVM currently reads / writes ~25GB/s to RAM which is approaching limits on most motherboards.

excerpts.author: vladimir_ea
excerpts.content: so such large operators would need to be able to partition this work across multiple machines.

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content: oh, I didn't know about that limitation

excerpts.author: vladimir_ea
excerpts.content: it seems like for both the leaf aggregations and the 16->1 it should be safe to use 'outside help' if it is available. Source the attestation aggregate from a large operator / provider - take the intersection of the attestations / clams you have and the aggregate has - verify the proof with the declared claims - this last produces a new proof but it is much faster then aggregating (~200ms or similar).
